## Introduction: 


### Data Acquisition- State Electricity Profiles
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```

#### Energy Consumption (NTD Energy Usage)
```{r}
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```

#### Transit Service Provided

```{r}
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```
## Recoding the Mode Column
```{r}
# List the unique transit mode codes used in the energy data
NTD_ENERGY |> distinct(Mode)

# Translate NTD's two-letter mode codes into readable names.
# Codes and meanings come from the NTD glossary.
recode_mode <- function(x) {
  recode_values(x,
    "AR" ~ "Alaska Railroad",
    "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
    "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
    "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
    "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
    "DT" ~ "Demand Response Taxi",
    "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
    "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
    "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
    "JT" ~ "Jitney",
    "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
    "MB" ~ "Bus",
    "MG" ~ "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
    "OR" ~ "Other Rail",
    "PB" ~ "Publico",
    "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
    "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",
    "TB" ~ "Trolleybus",
    "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
    "VP" ~ "Vanpool",
    "YR" ~ "Hybrid Rail",
    default = "Unknown"
  )
}

# Apply the same translation to both NTD tables so they still match when joined
NTD_ENERGY  <- NTD_ENERGY  |> mutate(Mode = recode_mode(Mode))
NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |> mutate(mode = recode_mode(mode))
```
## Exploratory Data analysis

The problem was the data had 2 letter codes and there are `r n_distinct(NTD_ENERGY$Mode)` different ones. For anyone that is not familiar with what each means its hard to understand so I renamed the. I found them with distinct(), then built one function and used it so the two tables NTD_Energy and NTD_Service can be matched on mode later since the labels on both have to be identical. The most agency mode rows in the data set was Bus and Demand response.


#### EDA EIA State Electricity Profiles

```{r}
# Packages for formatted tables and number formatting
library(gt)
library(scales)
```
1. Which 5 states have the most expensive retail electricity? 
```{r}
# The 5 states with the highest average retail electricity price
expensive_states <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(electricity_price_MWh, n = 5)

ggplot(expensive_states,
       aes(x = reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh),
           y = electricity_price_MWh)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  labs(
    title = "States with the Most Expensive Electricity",
    subtitle = "Average retail price per MWh",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Price ($ per MWh)",
    caption = "Source: EIA State Electricity Profiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```
We can see that `r expensive_states$state[1]` is the state with the highest expensive Retail Electricity with `r dollar(expensive_states$electricity_price_MWh[1])`, followed by `r expensive_states$state[2]` with `r dollar(EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(state == "California") |> pull(electricity_price_MWh))`, `r expensive_states$state[3]`, `r expensive_states$state[4]`, and `r expensive_states$state[5]` with `r dollar(expensive_states$electricity_price_MWh[5])`.


2. Which 5 states have the ‘dirtiest’ electricity mix? (Table)

```{r}
# The 5 states with the highest CO2 emitted per MWh of electricity produced
dirtiest_states <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(CO2_MWh, n = 5) |>
  select(state, primary_source, CO2_MWh, electricity_price_MWh)

dirtiest_states |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "States with the Dirtiest Electricity",
    subtitle = "Pounds of CO2 emitted per MWh generated"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    state = "State",
    primary_source = "Primary Source",
    CO2_MWh = "CO2 (lbs/MWh)",
    electricity_price_MWh = "Price ($/MWh)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(CO2_MWh, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_currency(electricity_price_MWh, decimals = 2) |>
  tab_source_note(md("Source: EIA State Electricity Profiles."))
```

Here we can see the 5 states have the ‘dirtiest’ electricity mix are West Virginia with `r comma(dirtiest_states$CO2_MWh[1])`, Kentucky with `r comma(dirtiest_states$CO2_MWh[2])`, Wyoming with `r comma(dirtiest_states$CO2_MWh[3])`, Missouri with `r comma(dirtiest_states$CO2_MWh[4])`, and Hawaii with `r comma(dirtiest_states$CO2_MWh[5])`.

3. On average, how many pounds of CO2 are emitted per MWh of electricity produced in the US? 

```{r}

# Weight each state's CO2 rate by how much electricity it generates,
# so big producers like Texas count more than small ones like Vermont
us_avg_co2 <- weighted.mean(EIA_SEP_REPORT$CO2_MWh,
                            EIA_SEP_REPORT$generation_MWh)
```

On average `r comma(us_avg_co2, accuracy = 1)` pounds of CO2 are emitted per Mwh of electricity produced in the United States.

5. My home state, Texas, has a reputation as being the home of “dirty fossil fuels” while NY has a reputation as a leader in clean energy. How many times cleaner is NY’s energy mix than that of Texas? 
```{r}

# How many times more CO2 per MWh Texas emits compared with New York
tx_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "TX") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
ny_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "NY") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
ny_cleaner <- tx_co2 / ny_co2
```

NY's energy mix is `r comma(ny_co2)` pounds of CO₂ per MWh, Texas energy mix is `r comma(tx_co2)` pounds of CO₂ per MWh, and NY's energy mix is `r number(ny_cleaner, accuracy = 0.01)` pounds of CO₂ per MWh times cleaner than the energy mix in Texas.


#EDA - NTD Energy Usage

1. Which five transit agencies used the most gallons of fuel (all sources) and how did it breakdown by type?

What the code below does is leave out fuels that were not measured in gallons and then added the sum of all the gallons to create the list of the top 5 with the highest total combined of gallon usage.

```{r}
# Fuel columns measured in gallons (electricity is in kWh and hydrogen in kg,
# so they can't be added to gallons and are left out here)
gallon_cols <- c("Gallons of Bio-Diesel", "Gallons of Bunker Fuel",
                 "Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas", "Gallons of Diesel Fuel",
                 "Gallons of Ethanol", "Gallons of Gasoline", "Gallons of Kerosene",
                 "Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas", "Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas")

# Add up each agency's fuel across all its modes, then keep the 5 biggest users
top_fuel_agencies <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(across(all_of(gallon_cols), sum), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(total_gallons = rowSums(across(all_of(gallon_cols)))) |>
  slice_max(total_gallons, n = 5)

top_fuel_agencies |>
  select(`Agency Name`, total_gallons, `Gallons of Diesel Fuel`,
         `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, `Gallons of Gasoline`) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Transit Agencies Using the Most Fuel",
    subtitle = "Gallons of combustion fuel, all modes combined"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    `Agency Name` = "Agency",
    total_gallons = "Total",
    `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` = "Diesel",
    `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` = "CNG",
    `Gallons of Gasoline` = "Gasoline"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(-`Agency Name`, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_source_note(md("Source: National Transit Database, 2025 Energy Consumption."))
```

The top 5 agencies that used the most gallons of fuel where 	`r top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][1]` with `r comma(top_fuel_agencies$total_gallons[1])` total gallons, `r top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][2]`, `r top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][3]`, `r top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][4]`, `r top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][5]` with `r comma(top_fuel_agencies$total_gallons[5])` gallons. 

In all agencies diesel was the most gallon-basedused type of energy except for `r top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][3]` that used `r comma(top_fuel_agencies[["Gallons of Diesel Fuel"]][3])` diesel and on the contrary used the highest amount of CNG with `r comma(top_fuel_agencies[["Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas"]][3])`. For 	`r top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][4]` this is the only agency that relies solely on diesel when it comes to gallon-based fuels, and uses no other types of gallon- based energy, while   `r paste(top_fuel_agencies[["Agency Name"]][c(1, 2, 5)], collapse = ", ")` use diesel, CNG, and gasoline.


2. Across all US public transit, visualize the amounts of each type of fuel used:

```{r}
# Total gallons of each fuel across all US transit agencies
fuel_totals <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  summarize(across(all_of(gallon_cols), sum)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "fuel", values_to = "gallons") |>
  mutate(fuel = str_remove(fuel, "Gallons of "))

ggplot(fuel_totals, aes(x = reorder(fuel, gallons), y = gallons)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  labs(
    title = "Fuel Used by US Public Transit",
    subtitle = "Total gallons by fuel type, 2025",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Gallons (millions)",
    caption = "Source: National Transit Database, 2025 Energy Consumption"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot")

# Values referenced in the text
diesel_gallons    <- fuel_totals |> filter(fuel == "Diesel Fuel") |> pull(gallons)
diesel_share      <- diesel_gallons / sum(fuel_totals$gallons)

cng_gallons       <- fuel_totals |> filter(fuel == "Compressed Natural Gas") |> pull(gallons)
cng_share         <- cng_gallons / sum(fuel_totals$gallons)

gas_gallons       <- fuel_totals |> filter(fuel == "Gasoline") |> pull(gallons)
gas_share         <- gas_gallons / sum(fuel_totals$gallons)

biodiesel_gallons <- fuel_totals |> filter(fuel == "Bio-Diesel") |> pull(gallons)
biodiesel_share   <- biodiesel_gallons / sum(fuel_totals$gallons)
```
We can see in the graph above that Diesel Fuel was the most used overall by US Public Transit with `r comma(diesel_gallons, scale = 1e-6, accuracy = 1, suffix = " million")` gallons. The second most used was Compressed Natural Gas with `r comma(cng_gallons, scale = 1e-6, accuracy = 1, suffix = " million")` gallons, and the third was Gasoline with `r comma(gas_gallons, scale = 1e-6, accuracy = 1, suffix = " million")` gallons. Overall, diesel had `r percent(diesel_share, accuracy = 0.1)` share of the amount of gallons used which is more than half of the gallon based energy. Compressed natural gas had a `r percent(cng_share, accuracy = 0.1)` share of the amount of gallons, and the rest of the shares are divided into the remaining of the gallon-based energies in smaller shares. 

# EDA - NTD Service 

1. Which five transit services have the most UPT annually?

```{r}
# Combine rows that share the same agency + mode (they are split by type of service),
# then keep the 5 services with the most unlinked passenger trips
top_upt <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, mode) |>
  summarize(total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(total_upt, n = 5) |>
  mutate(
    short_name = str_remove(AGENCY, ", dba:.*"),          # drop the ", dba: ..." part
    service    = str_wrap(paste0(short_name, " (", mode, ")"), width = 30)  # wrap long labels
  )

ggplot(top_upt, aes(x = reorder(service, total_upt), y = total_upt)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(scale = 1e-9, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = "B")) +
  labs(
    title = "US Transit Services with the Most Trips",
    subtitle = "Unlinked passenger trips (UPT), 2025",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Trips (billions)",
    caption = "Source: National Transit Database, 2025 Service by Agency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot")

# Values referenced in the text
top_service     <- top_upt$short_name[1]
top_service_upt <- top_upt$total_upt[1]
```

The transit service with the most UPT annually was `r top_service`with the mode being `r top_upt$mode[1]` and the total subway trips being: `r comma(top_service_upt, scale = 1e-9, accuracy = 0.01, suffix = " billion")`. Second place was also `r top_upt$short_name[2]` with the mode being `r top_upt$mode[2]`. The rest of the US transit services with the most UPT were: `r top_upt$short_name[3]`, `r top_upt$short_name[4]`, and `r top_upt$short_name[5]`.

2. What is the average trip length of a trip on MTA NYC? 

```{r}
# "MTA" matches agencies outside New York too (Maryland, Flint), and the MTA's own
# agencies are listed under different cities, so check before filtering
NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(str_detect(AGENCY, "MTA")) |>
  distinct(AGENCY, city)
```

```{r}
# Average trip length on MTA New York City Transit (all its modes combined):
# total passenger miles divided by total trips
mta_nyct <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(AGENCY == "MTA New York City Transit")

mta_avg_trip <- sum(mta_nyct$sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE) /
                sum(mta_nyct$total_upt, na.rm = TRUE)

# Average trip length by mode, for reference in the text
mta_by_mode <- mta_nyct |>
  group_by(mode) |>
  summarize(avg_trip = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE) /
                       sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE))

subway_trip <- mta_by_mode |> filter(mode == "Heavy Rail") |> pull(avg_trip)
bus_trip    <- mta_by_mode |> filter(mode == "Bus") |> pull(avg_trip)
```

The average trip length on the MTA NYC is `r number(mta_avg_trip, accuracy = 0.01)` miles in all modes, `r number(subway_trip, accuracy = 0.01)` miles in subway, and `r number(bus_trip, accuracy = 0.01)` miles in bus.

### Data Integration

# Joining Data Files

About 561,675,933 were recorded in states where the primary energy source was nuclear power.

#### Data Analysis 

## Calculating Total Emissions

Here we combine the three tables NTD_SERVICE, NTD_ENERGY, and EIA_SEP_REPORT together to be able to get the CO2 associated with each agency and mode. 

```{r}
# NTD_SERVICE has several rows per agency + mode (split by type of service), so add
# them up first. Also convert the ID from text ("00001") to a number to match NTD_ENERGY.
service_by_mode <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = as.numeric(NTD_ID)) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, state, mode) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt       = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
# Join 1: fuel use + ridership, matched on agency ID AND mode (inner: need both)
# Join 2: + each state's CO2 per MWh for electric vehicles (inner: 50 states only)
emissions <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  inner_join(service_by_mode, join_by(`NTD ID` == NTD_ID, Mode == mode)) |>
  inner_join(EIA_SEP_REPORT |> select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh),
             join_by(state == abbreviation))
```

```{r}
# EIA CO2 conversion factors (pounds of CO2 per gallon), from
# https://www.eia.gov/environment/emissions/co2_vol_mass.php
CO2_DIESEL   <- 22.45   # also used for bio-diesel
CO2_RESIDUAL <- 24.78   # bunker fuel
CO2_GASOLINE <- 18.73   # finished motor gasoline, also used for ethanol
CO2_KEROSENE <- 21.78
CO2_PROPANE  <- 12.68   # liquified petroleum gas
CO2_CNG      <- 120.85 * 0.12667   # natural gas per Mcf x Mcf per gallon equivalent
CO2_LNG      <- 120.85 * 0.0826    # natural gas per Mcf x Mcf per gallon of LNG

emissions <- emissions |>
  mutate(
    total_co2_lbs =
      (`Gallons of Diesel Fuel` + `Gallons of Bio-Diesel`) * CO2_DIESEL +
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel`                             * CO2_RESIDUAL +
      (`Gallons of Gasoline` + `Gallons of Ethanol`)       * CO2_GASOLINE +
      `Gallons of Kerosene`                                * CO2_KEROSENE +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`                 * CO2_PROPANE +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`                  * CO2_CNG +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`                       * CO2_LNG +
      # electricity: kWh -> MWh (divide by 1000) x the state's lbs CO2 per MWh
      (`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` +
         `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`) / 1000 * CO2_MWh,
    total_co2_tons = total_co2_lbs / 2000   # 2,000 lbs = 1 short ton
  )
```

I used inner_join to merge NTD_ENERGY with service_by_mode and then I merged that with EIA_SEP_REPORT. I joined them using inner_join because I needed ridership and fuel to compute the emissions. The Emissions were computed by multiplying each fuel with its EIA CO2 fuel factors data found in the EIA link [EIA's CO2 emissions coefficients](https://www.eia.gov/environment/emissions/co2_vol_mass.php).

Then the Electricity Emissions was computed by converting kWh to MWh (1MWh=1,000kWh) and then multiplying the MWh from NTD_ENERGY by the states CO2 per MWh that could be found in the EIA_SEP_REPORT. The fuel and electricity emissions are added for the total.

#### Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage (Emissions per trip and per mile)

```{r}
# Combine each agency's modes, then compute emissions per trip and per passenger mile.
# Very small agencies (under 100,000 trips a year) are dropped because their ratios
# swing wildly, and the rest are grouped by size so they compete with similar agencies.
agency_emissions <- emissions |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`, state) |>
  summarize(
    total_co2_lbs   = sum(total_co2_lbs),
    total_upt       = sum(total_upt),
    passenger_miles = sum(passenger_miles),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(total_upt >= 100000, passenger_miles > 0) |>
  mutate(
    co2_per_trip = total_co2_lbs / total_upt,          # lbs of CO2 per trip
    co2_per_mile = total_co2_lbs / passenger_miles,    # lbs of CO2 per passenger mile
    size = case_when(
      total_upt < 1e6 ~ "Small",    # 100k to 1 million trips a year
      total_upt < 2e7 ~ "Medium",   # 1 to 20 million
      TRUE            ~ "Large"     # 20 million or more
    )
  )

# Most efficient agency in each size group (lowest CO2 per passenger mile)
agency_emissions |>
  group_by(size) |>
  slice_min(co2_per_mile, n = 3) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(size = factor(size, levels = c("Small", "Medium", "Large"))) |>
  arrange(size, co2_per_mile) |>
  select(size, `Agency Name`, state, total_upt, co2_per_trip, co2_per_mile) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "size") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Most Efficient Transit Agencies by Size",
    subtitle = "Lowest pounds of CO2 per passenger mile, 2025"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    `Agency Name` = "Agency",
    state = "State",
    total_upt = "Trips",
    co2_per_trip = "CO2 per Trip (lbs)",
    co2_per_mile = "CO2 per Mile (lbs)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(total_upt, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(c(co2_per_trip, co2_per_mile), decimals = 3) |>
  tab_source_note(md("Sources: National Transit Database (2025); EIA State Electricity Profiles; EIA CO2 coefficients."))

# Greenest agency in each size group, for the awards
greenest <- agency_emissions |>
  group_by(size) |>
  slice_min(co2_per_mile, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
# Greenest agency overall (lowest CO2 per passenger mile across all sizes)
overall_greenest <- agency_emissions |> slice_min(co2_per_mile, n = 1)
```

In the table above we can see the breakdown of the most efficient transit agencies by size after adding up each agency's modes (small-medium-large). We can also see the state they are in, the CO2 per trip, and the CO2 per mile. If the agency had 100k to 1 million trips it was categorized as small, if it had 1 million to 20 million trips it was categorized as medium, and if it had 20 million trips and above it was categorized large. The small agencies under 100k trips were not included in the analysis because the data is not reliable because it had wide variations and contained very few trips.

The data was grouped by size and divided by trips, and miles to be able to evaluate the efficiency of the transit agencies regardless of the size. Measuring the emissions per mile shows the efficiency of each agency and prevents the large agencies from being incorrectly labeled the least green just because of the volume they have, but show the efficiency of agencies in other size ranges.

##Award Winners ( Greenest Transit Agencies)

```{r}
# Reference values for the awards
median_co2_per_mile <- median(agency_emissions$co2_per_mile)   # the typical agency

# A new car meeting the US fuel economy (CAFE) standard for model year 2026 gets about
# 49 miles per gallon, so a solo driver emits the gasoline CO2 factor / 49 per mile
CAFE_MPG         <- 49
car_co2_per_mile <- CO2_GASOLINE / CAFE_MPG

# "Worst of" award: the state whose public transit emits the most CO2
# per passenger mile, with all of its agencies combined
state_efficiency <- agency_emissions |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarize(
    total_co2_lbs   = sum(total_co2_lbs),
    passenger_miles = sum(passenger_miles),
    n_agencies      = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(co2_per_mile = total_co2_lbs / passenger_miles) |>
  filter(n_agencies >= 3)          # skip states with too few agencies to judge fairly

worst_state <- state_efficiency |> slice_max(co2_per_mile, n = 1)
```

Award 1:  Greenest Transit Agency Award (by size and overall): 

The most efficient agency with the least CO2 per mile in the small category was `r greenest[["Agency Name"]][greenest$size == "Small"]` with `r number(greenest$co2_per_mile[greenest$size == "Small"], accuracy = 0.001)` pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile. The most efficient agency in the medium category was `r greenest[["Agency Name"]][greenest$size == "Medium"]` with `r number(greenest$co2_per_mile[greenest$size == "Medium"], accuracy = 0.001)` pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile. Finally, the most efficient agency in the large category was `r greenest[["Agency Name"]][greenest$size == "Large"]` with `r number(greenest$co2_per_mile[greenest$size == "Large"], accuracy = 0.001)` pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile. The greenest and most efficient transit agency overall was `r overall_greenest[["Agency Name"]]` with `r number(overall_greenest$co2_per_mile, accuracy = 0.001)` pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile. For reference here is the median for the agencies efficiency `r number(median_co2_per_mile, accuracy = 0.001)` pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile. This means the winner of this award is `r number(median_co2_per_mile / overall_greenest$co2_per_mile, accuracy = 0.1)` times greener than the median!

Award 2: The Worst State whose public transit emits the most CO2 per passenger mile

The state whose agencies emit the most amount of CO2 per passenger mile is `r state.name[match(worst_state$state, state.abb)]` with `r number(worst_state$co2_per_mile, accuracy = 0.01)` pounds of CO2 per passenger mile and `r comma(worst_state$total_co2_lbs / 2000, accuracy = 1)` tons of CO2. To put this in perspective a solo driver in a car has `r number(car_co2_per_mile, accuracy = 0.01)` pounds of CO₂ per passenger mile, which means the state of `r state.name[match(worst_state$state, state.abb)]` agencies are `r number(worst_state$co2_per_mile / car_co2_per_mile, accuracy = 0.1)` times less efficient and green than driving a new car that meets the CAFE standard (`r CAFE_MPG`) mpg solo instead of using public transportation. For this award only states with 3 or more agencies were compared.
